title: Operations
scenario: The board's funded fixes are merged into one branch and running on a live night. Then something happens that nobody planned for.
why: Fixes overlap and interact, and real nights bring events no test covered. Triage, an incident record and a runbook that matches the code are what keep the next night from going silent.
objective: Triage a live event on the funded portfolio, write an incident record with a root cause, update the night cover runbook, and decide whether a hotfix is needed.

tools.name: incident-response
tools.for: Structures triage, diagnosis, mitigation and root cause. It's written for Azure, so use its structure and skip its Azure tooling

tools.name: Documentation
tools.for: Updates `data/runbook.md` so night cover steps match how the portfolio behaves

tools.name: RPI Agent
tools.for: Takes a hotfix through research, plan and implement, as in chapter 08

steps: Watch the trainer's screen while an event plays into the running night. You see only its consequences.
Triage from [Alarms and incidents](/#/alarms) and the case charts: what is warm, who was told, and what night cover should do now.

steps.text: Run `/incident-response` with this prompt. Fill in triage, diagnosis, mitigation and root cause, and skip its Azure steps: this app runs on your laptop.

prompt.label: Write the incident record
prompt.text: /incident-response For zava-silent-night: during tonight's run of the Board portfolio branch, (describe what you saw, with times from Alarms and incidents). Phase is triage. This is a local training app, so skip the Azure tooling and use only the triage, diagnosis, mitigation and root-cause structure. Write the incident record to `docs/incident-response/zava-silent-night-chaos-1.md`.

steps.text: Pick Documentation and send this prompt to update `data/runbook.md` so night cover would act correctly next time. Keep the synthetic label in its first lines.

prompt.label: Update the runbook
prompt.text: Update `data/runbook.md` for zava-silent-night so the night cover steps match how the funded fixes behave, based on the incident record at `docs/incident-response/zava-silent-night-chaos-1.md`. Keep the synthetic label in the first lines and keep the runbook short.

steps.text: If the root cause is a gap in the code, decide on a hotfix and start it in RPI Agent with this prompt, as in chapter 08.

prompt.label: Start a hotfix
prompt.text: Start a hotfix for zava-silent-night from the incident record at `docs/incident-response/zava-silent-night-chaos-1.md`. Work through each phase with me. Write the research under `.copilot-tracking/research/`, write failing tests first, and keep every existing test passing.

ask: What did night cover see first, and what should they have done?
Which funded fix should have caught this, and did it?
Does the runbook match the code now?
Is this a hotfix tonight or a work item for the next sprint?
mistakes: Writing the root cause as a person's mistake
Changing code before writing down what happened
Leaving the runbook's line that defrosts always end after 30 minutes
step_in: When a table goes straight to a hotfix with no mitigation for tonight

before: During the 14:45 break, merge the funded branches into one branch, for example `board-portfolio`, with `/git-merge`. Run `python -m zava_cold_chain gauntlet --seed 2026 --team "Board portfolio" --fixes FX-1,FX-2` with your secret seed and the funded fixes, and copy the scorecard into `scorecards/`.
Start `python -m zava_cold_chain serve --scorecards scorecards` on that branch and replay `normal`, ready for a card.

Choose the card. Fleet defrost with no end time shows a funded alarm or guardrail fix working. Planned 40-minute vendor defrost tests that planned work still goes through without a page. A note that tells the assistant what to say tests the assistant decision. Door left open shows the original alarm still works.

run.do: Show the Board portfolio row on the leaderboard. Fixes overlap, so the combined result is less than the sum.
Play the chosen card from [Chaos cards](/#/chaos) into the running night. Say nothing about what it is.
Tables triage from Alarms and incidents and start their incident record.
Tables write the root cause, update the runbook and decide hotfix or follow-up.
Each table reads its root cause in one sentence. Then move to the debrief and case file reveal at 16:00.

facilitator.good_answer: An incident record with a timeline taken from the monitor, a root cause stated as a control that failed, a mitigation for tonight and a follow-up with an owner. A runbook that no longer says defrosts always end after 30 minutes. If the card was the planned 40-minute vendor defrost, a good portfolio lets it through without a page.
watch_for: Tables blaming the vendor or a person. There is no villain: every control assumed another control would catch it.
A runbook change that contradicts what the code does
facilitator.demo: If FX-1 or FX-2 was funded, play Fleet defrost with no end time on the Board portfolio branch and show the room the alarm or refusal that the Silent Night never had.

done_when: It has triage, diagnosis, mitigation and root cause sections
It records your table's decision: hotfix now or a follow-up with an owner
`data/runbook.md` is updated on your branch and still says synthetic in its first lines

stuck.then: Work from consequences: list everything that changed on Alarms and incidents and the case charts after the time the trainer played the card.
Tell it this is a local training app and to use only its triage, diagnosis, mitigation and root-cause structure.

stuck.if: There's no time for a hotfix
stuck.then: Record it in the incident record as a follow-up with an owner.

handoff.note: The debrief at 16:00 takes each table's root cause and the board's decisions.
